cause_quote: feat(browser): add MCP tool dispatch added `page.on("request", (req: Request) => { ... state.requestMap.set(req, entry) ... })`, a permanent Playwright Request subscription for the network log.
user_saw: Gateway memory grew steadily (about 8 MB/min of buffers in the measured workload) while an attached managed-browser page kept sending background POST requests.
summary: Replaced the permanent Playwright request/response/requestfailed page listeners with a bounded network metadata log fed from CDP messages the transport already receives.
reasoning: The leak comes from the page-level Playwright request listeners, which make Playwright materialize and retain Request dispatchers and POST buffers; GraphQL blame at the parent puts the current listener lines in refactor 425df19 (#149651), whose diff only moves the same pre-existing listeners, and full-history listing traces the listener design to fa54950 (2025-12-19), where `page.on("request")` first appears in src/browser/pw-session.ts. I could not confirm the lineage was continuous through later prunes or whether Playwright's dispatcher retention changed with a dependency upgrade (which would make this latent), so confidence is low.
